raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`amd/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Quark-MXFP4` crashes at load because its MXFP8 shared experts are fused into the packed MXFP4 routed-expert slot, so this PR makes the Quark fusion gate probe every named MoE layer and has the MiniMax-M3 hooks ask that gate.

```text
RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (384) must match the size of tensor b (768) at non-singleton dimension 1
```

`QuarkConfig.can_fuse_shared_expert()` compares routed and shared specs only at layer 0 and the NextN block. When layer 0 is a dense MLP (MiniMax-M3, DeepSeek-V3, GLM-5.x, Kimi-K2.x), both lookups fall back to the global spec and agree, whatever the MoE layers hold. The MiniMax-M3 hooks never ask the gate anyway: they refuse only `modelopt_mixed` and `minimax_m3_nvfp4`.

## Modifications

- `quark`: `can_fuse_shared_expert()` also probes every target decoder layer whose routed or shared experts are named in `layer_quant_config`, so one mismatched layer refuses fusion in any entry order. Draft entries (`mtp.*`, NextN layers past `num_hidden_layers`, non-`layers.<N>` bases such as `model.mtp.0`) are skipped, so an FP8 MTP block still vetoes fusion only for the draft.
- `minimax`: both MiniMax-M3 hooks call `quant_blocks_shared_experts_fusion(quant_config)`, as DeepSeek-V2/V3/V4 do. The name list stays because `MiniMaxM3Nvfp4Config` does not implement the gate.

The checkpoint now loads unfused and logs why, the path `--disable-shared-experts-fusion` selects today. Across 13 local Quark checkpoints only this one changes (fused → unfused); MiniMax-M3, GLM-5.x, DeepSeek-R1-0528, Kimi-K2.6, Muse-Spark and Qwen3.5 MXFP4 exports keep their decision.

Correct output also needs the MXFP8 scale handling from #46693, #46587 and #44080 (on `main` 2160 `weight_scale not found in params_dict`). #46587 instead requantizes the shared expert to MXFP4 to keep fusion; Quark leaves lossy conversion opt-in via `--enforce-shared-experts-fusion`.

## Accuracy Tests

4×MI355X, TP4, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, `main@6393e66b86` plus the same scale handling in every arm. GSM8K via `sglang.test.run_eval`, 5-shot chat, temperature 0, 1314 items.

| Arm | Load | GSM8K |
| --- | --- | --- |
| default | crash (fusion enabled) | — |
| `--disable-shared-experts-fusion` | ok | 0.9665, 0.9673 |
| this PR, default | ok, fusion disabled | 0.9627, 0.9665 |

Both loading arms run the same unfused path; differences are within noise (stderr ±0.005).

New tests in `test_quark_config.py` and `test_shared_experts_fusion_gates.py` cover dense leading layers, both entry orders, named routed experts, NextN drafts and a real `QuarkConfig` in M3.1's layout; 106 pass.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not a speed change: the fused path does not load on `main`.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). Not needed.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

nodes.body: @ZhengGong-amd _first_named_shared_expert_layer() makes this global fusion decision depend on quant-config insertion order. I reproduced this with the actual config helpers: routed experts use FP4, layer 3 shared experts use FP4, and layer 4 shared experts use FP8. Listing layer 3 first returns True; reversing the same entries returns False. The True case still enables fusion for the incompatible later layer. Could you check every distinct matching target-model MoE layer, or conservatively disable fusion when their schemes differ? One compact regression covering both entry orders should be enough.

Thanks, checking all named target MoE layers resolves the ordering and later-layer mixed-precision issues. The regression covers both entry orders and excludes draft layers. LGTM; please wait for the relevant quantization CI before merging.

+    def _named_moe_layers(self, layer_quant_config: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:

+class TestSharedExpertFusionGateDenseLeadingLayers(CustomTestCase):
+    """amd/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Quark-MXFP4 layout: the leading layers are dense
+    MLPs, the routed experts take the MXFP4 global spec, and every MoE layer
+    names its shared expert MXFP8 in layer_quant_config.
+
+    Layer 0 has neither routed nor shared experts, so both of its lookups fall
+    back to the global spec and agree. Fusing on that answer copies the MXFP8
+    shared expert into the packed MXFP4 slot, which fails at load.
+    """
+
+    _PREFIX = "language_model.model.layers"
+
+    def _config(
+        self,
+        shared_spec_by_layer,
+        prefix=_PREFIX,
+        num_hidden_layers=None,
+        num_nextn_predict_layers=0,
+    ) -> QuarkConfig:
+        config = _bare_config()
+        config.quant_config = {
+            "global_quant_config": deepcopy(_MXFP4_MOE_SPEC),
+            "layer_quant_config": {
+                f"{prefix}.0.self_attn.q_proj": deepcopy(_MXFP8_LINEAR_SPEC),
+                **{
+                    f"{prefix}.{layer}.mlp.shared_experts.{proj}": deepcopy(spec)
+                    for layer, spec in shared_spec_by_layer.items()
+                    for proj in ("gate_proj", "up_proj", "down_proj")
+                },
+            },
+            "layer_type_quant_config": {},
+        }
+        config.exclude_layers = []
+        config.packed_modules_mapping = {"gate_up_proj": ["gate_proj", "up_proj"]}
+        config.num_hidden_layers = num_hidden_layers
+        config.num_nextn_predict_layers = num_nextn_predict_layers

+            with self.subTest(prefix=prefix):
+                config = self._config(shared, prefix=prefix)
+                self.assertFalse(config.can_fuse_shared_expert())
+
+    def test_shared_expert_in_the_routed_format_still_fuses(self):
+        config = self._config({3: _MXFP4_MOE_SPEC, 4: _MXFP4_MOE_SPEC})
+        self.assertTrue(config.can_fuse_shared_expert())
+
+    def test_one_mismatched_moe_layer_blocks_fusion_in_any_entry_order(self):
+        for shared in (
+            {3: _MXFP4_MOE_SPEC, 4: _MXFP8_LINEAR_SPEC},
+            {4: _MXFP8_LINEAR_SPEC, 3: _MXFP4_MOE_SPEC},
+        ):
+            with self.subTest(order=list(shared)):
+                self.assertFalse(self._config(shared).can_fuse_shared_expert())
+
+    def test_named_routed_experts_in_another_format_block_fusion(self):
+        config = self._config({})
+        config.quant_config["layer_quant_config"][f"{self._PREFIX}.3.mlp.experts"] = (
+            deepcopy(_FP8_MOE_SPEC)
+        )
+        self.assertFalse(config.can_fuse_shared_expert())
+
+    def test_a_draft_layer_does_not_answer_for_the_target(self):
+        # The NextN layer appended after the decoder keeps its shared expert
+        # MXFP8; the target's own MoE layer matches its routed experts.
+        config = self._config(
+            {4: _MXFP8_LINEAR_SPEC, 3: _MXFP4_MOE_SPEC},
+            prefix="model.layers",
+            num_hidden_layers=4,
+            num_nextn_predict_layers=1,
+        )
+        self.assertTrue(config.can_fuse_shared_expert())
